claims: NASA is currently targeting 2027 for the launch of Artemis III.
Artemis III is designed to test rendezvous and docking capabilities between the Orion spacecraft and commercial lunar landers in low-Earth orbit.
Artemis III will focus on orbital demonstrations rather than an immediate lunar landing.
Artemis III is scheduled to launch in 2027.
The mission goal of Artemis III is to test systems like the Starship or Blue Moon landers and new EVA suits before a surface landing.
The launch vehicle for Artemis III is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center.
A crewed surface landing near the South Pole is now planned to follow Artemis III.
The next major mission is scheduled for 2028.
In early 2026, NASA revised the timeline to increase mission cadence and ensure safety.
NASA added an orbital test mission prior to the landing attempt.
As of April 2026, Artemis III is officially set for 2027.
